key_insight: C3PRO turns pathology foundation-model features into interpretable cell- and neighborhood-based phenotypes that match black-box MIL performance while giving pathologists auditable histologic explanations.
clinical_relevance: In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma biopsy slides, this approach could support diagnosis, survival risk, and resectability assessment with better transparency for clinical review.
method: Extracted cell-centered tile embeddings from a pathology foundation model
Clustered embeddings into recurring morphological phenotypes and built a spatial graph of phenotype motifs
Compared C3PRO with four MIL baselines and had expert pathologists annotate representative phenotype mosaics
evidence_signal: Evaluated with nested cross-validation on 809 patients (825 biopsies), where C3PRO achieved AUC 0.958 for diagnosis, 0.617 for survival, and 0.696 for resectability, on par with top MIL models.
watch_item: The phenotype vocabulary and statistical findings need external validation and workflow testing before routine clinical deployment, especially across sites and scanners.
paper_title: An interpretable cell-centric representation of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma matches multiple-instance learning for clinical outcomes and leads to novel pathologist-driven histological biomarkers
